It was Adli, another replacement, who applied a delicate garnish.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionQuick GuideConference League: Salah breaks Hearts and Brighton held by JablonecShowInjury-hitHeartsproduced a spirited display in Turkey but ultimately went down to a 2-0 Conference League defeat at the hands of Mohamed Salah-inspiredTrabzonspor.The Scottish side acquitted themselves well amid a hostile atmosphere before going down to Salah’s first-half penalty and a second-half strike from Franculino, laid on by the former Liverpool star (pictured).The defeat leaves Wouter Vrancken’s side with one point from two matches ahead of their trip to Swiss champions Thun in a fortnight. Their visit had started in painful fashion after left-back Harry Milne suffered a suspected anterior cruciate ligament injury during training.Brightondrew a rare blank as they were held to a goalless draw by Czech minnowsJablonec. The Premier League’s top scorers, who have scored 23 goals across their first seven matches, misfired badly in the foothills of the Jizera Mountains in northern Czechia.Brighton head coach Fabian Hürzeler, in his 100th match in charge, made eight changes from that memorable win with only Bart Verbruggen, Olivier Boscagli and Pascal Gross keeping their places. The visitors squandered a host of chances, the best falling to Jack Hinshelwood, Georginio Rutter and Ibrahim Osman, and Jablonec were looking the likelier to score towards the end.Antonín Rusek almost capitalised on a mistake by Joao Costinha before Verbruggen had to make a spectacular fingertip save to prevent Jiri Slama’s drive from hitting the top corner.Press AssociationPhotograph: Hasan Tascan/AnadoluWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.What a night, then, for a club that knows what it is to gaze into the abyss. “How did we end up here?” asked the public address announcer before kick-off, a question repeated on a banner hoisted by the Steve Fletcher Stand, but it was worth posing in a different sense too. The sizable elephant in the room was how the Premier League’s 15th-placed team could face down one of Serie A’s most decorated institutions, unbeaten domestically this season, and simply sweep them off the park.In truth nobody could feign too much surprise; certainly not the bookmakers, who deemed Bournemouth the pre-match favourites. Scoffing at Milan’s inadequacy is, up to a point, simply plucking low-hanging fruit. Football’s ecosystem has arrived in a glum place where outwardly fairytale occasions like this are packaged with caveats: even the English top flight’s relative minnows are, through financial and physical power, playing on a different pitch to representatives of leagues once deemed its equals.For those understandably immersed in the here and now, Rayan came close to a superb fourth. “I’m happy for our fans especially,” Rose said. It is unlikely to be Bournemouth’s last European gala show.Explore more on these topicsEuropa LeagueBournemouthMilanmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Super Bowl contenders: are the NFL’s unbeaten teams as perfect as they seem? | NFL | The Guardian
description: The early standouts have emerged. But even the best teams have flaws that can be exposed by their opponents
Author: Graham Searles
Headline: The early standouts have emerged. But even the best teams have flaws that can be exposed by their opponents
Content: Patrick Mahomes greets Chiefs fans after yet another win.Photograph: Jamie Squire/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenPatrick Mahomes greets Chiefs fans after yet another win.Photograph: Jamie Squire/Getty ImagesNFLSuper Bowl contenders: are the NFL’s unbeaten teams as perfect as they seem?The early standouts have emerged. But even the best teams have flaws that can be exposed by their opponentsGraham SearlesThu 22 Oct 2026 04.30 EDTLast modified on Thu 22 Oct 2026 14.03 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSan Francisco 49ers (6-0)Who would have thought the 49ers would be here after a rough old offseason? Head coach Kyle Shanahan’s participation in training camp was limiteddue to a serious car crash, team owner Jed York’s visit to an Ohio trailer parkdid not end well, and one player after another endured serious injuries. Despite all this, San Francisco are full of positive vibes. They are top of a tough division and their immense defense, led by the intensity of players such as safety Malik Mustapha and Fred Warner, is complemented by an equally impressive offense.Troy Aikman and Joe Buck: what next for the NFL’s $165m TV power couple as they head for a split?Read moreBrock Purdy’srecord-setting quarterback ratinghas grabbed the headlines – and rightly so, as his laser accuracy on aggressive downfield throws sets the 49ers offense apart. But there are warnings Purdy’s offensive surge may not last. Pablo Torre pretty muchdebunkedthe 49ers’ electrical substation conspiracy theory, but injuries are piling up in the receiving corps. The team have four wide receivers on injured reserve, plus Brandon Aiyuk,who is in self-imposed exile. Purdy had found relief in the form of future Hall of Famer Mike Evans, but the 33-year-old left Monday’s win over the Washington Commanders with achilles pain and is also dealing with fractured ribs. And when Evans is off the field, Purdy struggles. On Monday, Evans caught three passes for 94 yards as the Niners appeared to be cruising at half-time. Without him, the offense went three and out three times, and only just hung on to beat the Commanders.The three-game lead the 49ers have in the NFC West should see them walk into the playoffs. But if Purdy can’t find healthy, reliable targets, the Niners will see another promising campaign end against the big boys in the postseason.Verdict:not quite the real thingKansas City Chiefs (5-0)The Chiefs are back. After they limped to a 6-11 finish last season, their record is spotless, and the AFC West – thanks in part to the Los Angeles Chargers’ implosion – already looks sewn up. Patrick Mahomes is back from the ACL tear he suffered in 2025, and the offense is no longer solely relying on the quarterback to paper over the cracks: the acquisition of running back Kenneth Walker III looks to be the move of the offseason. It was likely that last season’s Super Bowl MVP would be a solid get for a Chiefs rushing attack that averageda sluggish 4.2 yards per carrylast season. But Walker’s production has made the Seattle Seahawks look a little foolish to let him go.Kansas City picked him up for $14.35m a year, making him only the ninth-most expensive running back in the league. Did the Chiefs think Walker would be the NFL’s leading rusher coming into Week 7? Unlikely, especially as the Chiefs have already had their bye week. His 665 rushing yards still top the charts,as do the team’s 5.5 yards per carry. Walker’s penchant for explosive big plays has been the biggest transformation for Kansas City. He already has seven carries of more than 20 yards. The Chiefs managed just three all of last year.The knock on Kansas City is that Walker’s rampage has come amid a soft schedule to start the season. But if he overpowers his former employers – and their formidable defense – on Sunday night the rest of the league should be very worried.Verdict:the real thingMinnesota Vikings (5-0)The Vikings have an important talent when it comes to going the distance: the ability to win ugly. The Seahawks pulled off the same trick last season on the way to winning the Super Bowl. Now Minnesota are doing the same thing with a similarly dominant defense leading the charge. How important is the defense to the Vikings? They are the first team to go 4-0 while not scoring an offensive touchdown in multiple games (wins over Miami and Chicago) since the Detroit Lions in 1934.Perhaps more importantly for the Vikings’ championship hopes: their offense has shown signs of waking up. In their last game, a 23-13 victory over the Saints before the bye week, Kyler Murray had his best day in purple and gold. He looked reliable as the team’s starting quarterback, with an 80% completion rate, 229 passing yards and a highlight-reel touchdown throw that Justin Jefferson caught in triple coverage. As is the case with Evans and the 49ers, Jefferson unlocks a much higher level of production from Murray. The difference for the Vikings is their defense is a cut above the 49ers’ unit. They aren’t one of the best defenses – they arethebest. Brian Flores’s blitz-heavy package led by Dallas Turner on the edge and linebacker Blake Cashman has conceded just five touchdowns so far.Verdict:the real thingBuffalo Bills (5-1)OK, the Bills have lost a game, but we’re throwing them in here as they’ve been the best of the rest. You have to admire Josh Allen’s fondness for high drama – and his defense-shredding talent even more. Buffalo lead the league in scoring with four of their five wins coming in box-office shootouts. It’s never dull on the other side of the ball either: Buffalo’s defensehas allowed the most yards per game(386.8) of anyone in the league, bar the leaky Lions.View image in fullscreenJosh Allen celebrates with fans after the team’s win over the Raiders.Photograph: John Locher/APThe question is whether having such an abject defense is sustainable for the rest of the season. One key metric – stopping teams on third down – suggests they are in for a rough ride against elite opposition in the playoffs. What’s worse is that they started the season poorly in that category and have gotten progressively worse. TheNFLaverage for stops on third down is about 40%. In Week 2, the Lions were successful on third down 36% of the time against the Bills. Last Sunday the Raiders had 58% success in the same scenario. With Allen at the controls, the Bills will always have a shot; it’s just a shame he can’t play both ways. Buffalo need to function at a higher level on defense in fundamental areas to win it all.Verdict:not the real thingBonus category: the No 1 pick will go to …The Jets have a few shots at “glory”. Their three first-round picks are owned by 2-4 teams: the Colts, Cowboys and the Jets themselves. However, that trio are part of a bunch of franchises with two wins. Many would have been surprised to see the Philadelphia Eagles among those nine teams, but they could sink further. The ongoingsagaover Jalen Hurts’s blood clots means the untested Tanner McKee is now the team’s starting quarterback and the Eagles are dealing with a huge injury list. It’s not impossible to imagine they could be in play for the No 1 pick by the end of the season.However, much more likely to be picking first in 2027 are the winless Chargers and Dolphins. Miami are the solid choice to pick first. Their offense has been abysmal, except for one quarter of fluency under zero pressure from the Cincinnati Bengals. Sunday’s matchup will probably highlight the huge gulf in class between the merely bad Jets and the pit of despair that is the Dolphins.Explore more on these topicsNFLKansas City ChiefsSan Francisco 49ersMinnesota VikingsUS sportsBuffalo BillsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Welcome to the trap: swaggering Atlanta Dream turn WNBA finals into a hometown spectacle | WNBA | The Guardian
description: Atlanta’s hip-hop royalty brought the star power as the Dream turned their long-awaited WNBA finals homecoming into a celebration of everything the city does best
Author: Andrew Lawrence
Headline: Atlanta’s hip-hop royalty brought the star power as the Dream turned their long-awaited WNBA finals homecoming into a celebration of everything the city does best
Content: Angel Reese and her Atlanta Dream teammates celebrate after their 97-71 victory over the Golden State Valkyries in Game 3 of the WNBA finals on Wednesday night at State Farm Arena.Photograph: Kevin C Cox/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenAngel Reese and her Atlanta Dream teammates celebrate after their 97-71 victory over the Golden State Valkyries in Game 3 of the WNBA finals on Wednesday night at State Farm Arena.Photograph: Kevin C Cox/Getty ImagesWNBAWelcome to the trap: swaggering Atlanta Dream turn WNBA finals into a hometown spectacleAtlanta’s wounded sports fans know better than to get carried away. But the Dream’s first WNBA finals game in 13 years showed this might finally be a team worth falling forAndrew Lawrenceat State Farm ArenaThu 22 Oct 2026 05.00 EDTLast modified on Thu 22 Oct 2026 14.05 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTheAtlanta Dreamwere exactly where they wanted to be on Wednesday night, comfortably ensconced inside their downtown arena for Game 3 of the WNBA finals against theGolden State Valkyries. Kerry Washington, Ludacris and Cam Newton led the courtside celebrity delegation. Quavo and TI headlined the half-time show, while two more hugely popular Atlanta rappers performed during other extended play stoppages – a mini-spectacle that speaks to the city’s deep bench of hip-hop talent.Angel Reese stars again as Atlanta Dream thrash Valkyries to seize WNBA finals leadRead moreBut it was the crowd that really made State Farm Arena a house of horrors for Golden State. They didn’t just fill the 17,608-seat venue. They donned matching sky-blue T-shirts and waved rally towels. They sang along with their favorite emcees and lived and died with every point. They were so loud in the first quarter that I couldn’t hear the referee’s whistle from my 100-level press seat. They stayed to the end – well, two minutes from the buzzer anyway (gotta beat traffic) – and,with the 97-71 win sealedand DJ Khaled’s All I Do Is Win blasting through the arena speakers, serenaded the departing Valkyries with the unofficial Atlanta battle cry: “ATL hoe!”Angel Reesenever knew basketball could be like this. “When you can have at the end of the quarter a performance,” she gushed after a 21-point, 12-rebound effort. “And at the timeout, another performance. You smell the chicken, you smell the fish. It’s a blue-out in here. I didn’t even get to see Kerry. You don’t know who you gonna see in the A.”Quick GuideWNBA finals 2026ShowScheduleBest-of-seven series. All times Eastern.Sat 17 OctGame 1:Golden State 68, Atlanta 64Mon 19 OctGame 2:Atlanta 79, Golden State 65Wed 21 OctGame 3:Atlanta 97, Golden State 71Sat 24 OctGame 4: Golden State at Atlanta, 1pm (NBC)Mon 26 OctGame 5: Atlanta at Golden State, 8pm (USA/CNBC)Thu 29 OctGame 6: Golden State at Atlanta, 8pm* (USA/CNBC)Sat 31 OctGame 7: Atlanta at Golden State, 8pm* (USA/CNBC)*-if necessaryHow to watchIn the US, the series will air on NBC, USA Network and CNBC, with all games streaming on Peacock. In the UK, it will be carried by Sky Sports. In Australia, fans can watch through WNBA League Pass, with selected coverage also available through ESPN.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Atlanta has always been a strange sports town – one where fans learn not to fall too hard, lest they get burned by teams that either get ahead of themselves, self-destruct or wear out your patience with their underachievment. So fans proceed with apprehension. They find out-of-town teams to insulate themselves from disappointment, leave games early when defeat seems imminent and convince themselves they’re just beating traffic. They enjoy the music, the invitations to sing along andswag surf.View image in fullscreenAtlanta’s Isobel Borlase shoots over Golden State’s Kaitlyn Chen during the third quarter of Game 3 of the WNBA finals at State Farm Arena.Photograph: Kevin C Cox/Getty ImagesThe last time a playoff basketball game was played at State Farm Arena, theKnicks routed the Hawksto seal their Eastern Conference first-round series – and by the end, the New York fans had cleared out most of the Atlanta supporters and glitterati. With the Hawks down some 40 points, rappers Young Joc and Lil Boosie performed their hits for a crowd that half-bobbed along. It was hard to imagine the Atlanta sports scene getting more unserious.Then the Dreamreached the WNBA finals, only to learn theywouldn’t be able to play at State Farm Arena– their occasional home court. The Hawks, State Farm’s main tenant, were opening their season, while emo-pop artist Sombr had a gig scheduled. The Dream faced the possibility of hosting their first WNBA finals game in 13 years at the 3,500-seat airport arena where they played most of their home games, with neither the local college arenas nor the 13,000-seat suburban concert venue available. Gateway would have made for a jarring contrast with Chase Center – the NBA arena where the Valkyries’ passionate, violet-clad fans have createdBallhalla, one of the WNBA’s toughest places to play. The racial and economic makeup of the Atlanta and Golden State crowds would have surely added another dimension. But a combined effort by the teams, the league and the arena to bring the games to State Farm spared us that discourse.View image in fullscreenAtlanta rapper Quavo performs during the half-time show of Game 3.Photograph: Paras Griffin/Getty ImagesIt allowed Dream fans to show they can match that home-court advantage when Atlanta has a team worth believing in and the right venue. Three previous times the Dream have reached the finals, only for all three appearances to end in sweeps. But no one was thinking much about that on Wednesday night. Not with the Dream holding the Valkyries scoreless for the first five minutes before picking up where they left off in Game 2 and smothering them with their defense. Not with Reese jawing at the Valkyries bench after tough layups and, for good measure, setting off the crowd with a pair of open threes as her college coach,LSU’s Kim Mulkey, looked on in her blued-out pantsuit. Not with the Dream’s length and speed throwing a spanner into the Valkyries’ carefully choreographed offense, forcing Golden State to heave away at the basket late in the shot clock.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly for the 2026 WNBA seasonSign up toWNBA 30A limited run women’s basketball newsletter dedicated to the league’s historic 30th season.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionOnly thanks to three-point shooting from Cecilia Zandalasini and Gabby Williams did Golden State cut the deficit to six by half-time, then pulled level at 48 in the third quarter, with Zandalasini perfect beyond the arc to that point. Otherwise, a Valkyries team that prides itself on depth and balance was mostly caught off guard by a Dream team beating them at their own game while also doing what they do best: short-circuiting the pick-and-roll, winning extra possessions on steals and rebounds and scoring in transition.View image in fullscreenAtlanta’s Angel Reese celebrates after making a three-pointer against the Valkyries during the second quarter.Photograph: Kevin C Cox/Getty ImagesFormer No 1 draft pick Rhyne Howard, one of three Dream players named to the WNBA’s all-defensive team last week, became the first player to record five or more steals in consecutive finals games. Reese, the newly crowned defensive player of the year, became the youngest player in WNBA history to record a double-double in three straight finals games and joinedA’ja Wilsonas the only players to record at least 20 points and 10 rebounds in consecutive finals games. The Valkyries bench was a major factor again, outscoring the Dream reserves 38-27. But that advantage counted for little with Atlanta neutralizing Golden State starters Kiah Stokes, Veronica Burton and Kayla Thornton, who combined for five points on 2-of-11 shooting.When the final buzzer sounded, the Dream gathered at midcourt to drink in the atmosphere and toss mini balls into the stands, hard-won souvenirs for the sixth man who showed up and showed out. Hardly a Sombr crowd. And to think: if it hadn’t been fora sloppy final two minutes in Game 1, Atlanta would still have a perfect playoff record and be looking at a chance to clinch a title in Game 4 on Saturday in front of their fans. Instead, they’ll look to exploit their fearsome new home-court advantage for a shot at closing it out on Monday in California. If Golden State have Ballhalla, beware Atlanta: home of the trap.Explore more on these topicsWNBAAtlanta DreamGolden State ValkyriesAngel ReeseAtlantaCam NewtonKerry WashingtonfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Champions League review: PSG take a hit, Man City’s empty seats and teenage hope for Liverpool | Champions League | The Guardian
description: The reigning champions must deal with the absence of Khvicha Kvaratskhelia for some time, while fans at Anfield were thrilled by Rio Ngumoha
Author: John Brewin
Headline: The reigning champions must deal with the absence of Khvicha Kvaratskhelia for some time, while fans at Anfield were thrilled by Rio Ngumoha
Content: Phil Foden, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Rio Ngumoha made headlines this week.Composite: Getty, Reuters, ShutterstockView image in fullscreenPhil Foden, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Rio Ngumoha made headlines this week.Composite: Getty, Reuters, ShutterstockChampions LeagueChampions League review: PSG take a hit, Man City’s empty seats and teenage hope for LiverpoolThe reigning champions must deal with the absence of Khvicha Kvaratskhelia for some time, while fans at Anfield were thrilled by Rio NgumohaJohn BrewinThu 22 Oct 2026 09.42 EDTLast modified on Thu 22 Oct 2026 09.43 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleA big week for …Paris Saint-Germainbeat Barcelona 4-2 on Tuesday, but the reigning champions lost the best player in last season’s tournament, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. This autumn has seen much lobbying for the Ballon d’Or, with the Georgian a popular choice, despite his absence from the World Cup. He is expected to be out for six months, although Rodri’s comeback from serious injury – he was rested by Barcelona on Tuesday until coming off the bench in the 60th minute – shows it can take far longer than that for players to rediscover their highest level.“Why me?” Kvaratskhelia asked his Instagram followers. The PSG policy of resting players in Ligue 1 to save them for theChampions Leaguefailed to protect him. By resting Rodri, Barcelona followed a wider practice among major clubs in European competition of saving stars’ legs for big domestic occasions. Barcelona face Real Madrid this weekend though Lamine Yamal is not being spared; his brilliant goal in Paris made it 10 goals, matched by 10 assists, from 10 matches.Paris Saint-Germain sparkle on the pitch while the city of light burns around them | Barney RonayRead moreAnother heavyweight battle saw Arsenallose Bukayo Sakato a first-half quad injury inan entertaining 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich. Declan Rice powered in a late equalizer after Harry Kane had put on a show that included a goal and an assist. Does the Ballon d’Or beckon for Kane? The prediction markets suggest so.Matching Barcelona’s perfect record this season at home and abroad are Manchester City, who continue to thrive amid infamy. A resurgent Phil Foden scored a hat-trick and new signing Allan impressed. The official crowd fortheir 5-1 defeat of AEK Athenswas 40,402, but it looked smaller, and mockery duly descended on the club. There is mitigation for those who stayed away, including high ticket prices for Champions League matches in tough economic times, and a run of five home matches in 17 days. Still, City remain in the crosshairs, and the empty seats raise eyebrows for a club reporting record revenues. Equally, it is fair to point out that Anfield was not full, either, for Liverpool’s 4-3 defeat of Villarreal.A clean sweep of wins for Serie A, with three of their clubs scoring four goals. Inter let the side down with their 1-0 defeat of Shakhtar Donetsk. Roma defeated Slovan Bratislava 4-0, andComo beat Manchester United 4-1, but the game of the week came in Naples. Scott McTominay scored twice, his first goals since a procedure on a benign heart arrhythmia asNapoli beat Bodø/Glimt 4-3for their first win of the group stage. “I still need to find my best form, but I am not far away,” said McTominay.Player of the weekLiverpool were a mess in the first 30 minutes against Villarreal and it wasRio Ngumohawho led the recovery. The 18-year-old played off the right, supplying two assists with his left foot: the long-term replacement for Mohamed Salah may already be at Anfield.Liverpoolhave nursed Ngumoha along, though this was his fifth start of the season. “Everyone is chipping in but for him to work with Mo [Salah] last year was obviously massive,” Virgil van Dijk said of the teenager.Club in focus: ComoWith traditional Serie A giants Juventus and Milan in the Europa League, Como are enjoying their first season in the Champions League. IfManchester Unitedwere dreadful on Wednesday, Como’s rise hit its highest point yet. The club’s success carries echoes of Brighton and Bournemouth’s ascents, although Como’s is even more remarkable. They were a Serie D club in 2008, and the city is now known for something beyond its glorious scenery. Champions League winner Thierry Henry is among the investors in the club as is Como’s coach, Cesc Fàbregas, although the prime financiers are the Indonesian billionaire Hartono brothers.Jamestown Analytics, the Brighton owner Tony Bloom’s company, has been consultingComo. Arsène Wenger, Pep Guardiola, José Mourinho and Antonio Conte are the elite coaches Fàbregas played under, and he has forged a high-pressing style against Italian orthodoxy. As United labored, they were swarmed by Como’s worker bees. Real Madrid have a buy-back option for Nico Paz, bought by Como in 2024, and the scorer of two fine goals against United. Argentina’s latest Messi replacement is rather beefier than his country’s idol.As Como deepened Michael Carrick’s plight, thoughts moved to potential replacements. Fàbregas has been mentioned, though United fans will recall the summer of 2013’s unsuccessful chase for him. Had a deal been done, his midfield partner would have been … Carrick.View image in fullscreenNico Paz piled misery on Manchester United.Photograph: Kieran McManus/ShutterstockThey said itAnother week, another Manchester United PR crisis. This one involved Carrick hitting back at his players, a rarity in his managerial career. “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” Bruno Fernandes said.Carrick’s riposte: “If you don’t run and you don’t run forward and you don’t run back, you ain’t going to win.”On CBS, Jamie Carragher weighed, saying of Fernandes: “They all think he’s working hard. He’s not. He’s killing the rest of the team doing it.”The Amazon All or Nothing documentary series currently in production for United’s season will be appointment viewing.Looking aheadAfter two consecutive weeks of action, we have a fortnight off. Will Carrick still be at United by the time they host Roma on 3 November? Aston Villa, who have three wins from three and are second place in the table, have a glamour trip toBarcelona. Real Madrid, another side on three wins, travel to AEK.After defeat to Inter,Shakhtar’s adopted home, Stamford Bridge, hosts Sporting Lisbon, who this week were on the wrong end of Lask’s first ever group-stage win.Explore more on these topicsChampions LeagueParis Saint-GermainManchester UnitedBarcelonaComoManchester CityLiverpoolfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Haiti move Nations League home clash with USA to Miami amid gang violence crisis | Haiti football team | The Guardian
description: Unable to play on home soil amid a worsening security crisis, Haiti will host the US in Miami, where a large Haitian community promises a warm welcome
Author: Jeff Rueter
Headline: Unable to play on home soil amid a worsening security crisis, Haiti will host the US in Miami, where a large Haitian community promises a warm welcome
Content: Haiti’s Frantzdy Pierrot celebrates with teammates after scoring against New Zealand during an international friendly in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, in June.Photograph: Megan Briggs/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenHaiti’s Frantzdy Pierrot celebrates with teammates after scoring against New Zealand during an international friendly in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, in June.Photograph: Megan Briggs/Getty ImagesHaiti football teamHaiti move Nations League home clash with USA to Miami amid gang violence crisisConcacaf approves exceptional hosting arrangementHaiti to face US at Nu Stadium on 14 NovemberMiami’s Haitian community offers home advantageJeff RueterThu 22 Oct 2026 13.04 EDTLast modified on Thu 22 Oct 2026 14.58 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleConcacaf on Thursday announced it has approved Haiti’s request to relocate their Nations League quarter-final first leg against the United States on 14 November from Kingston, Jamaica, to Miami in an “exceptional hosting arrangement”. Haiti have been unable to play nominal “home” games within their borders since July 2021, withthe United Nations estimatingthat 90% of the capital of Port-au-Prince – including the national stadium – is controlled by violent gangs.Haiti’s match, the first leg of a home-and-away series against the US, had been booked for Kingston. The Grenadiers played their 2026 World Cup qualifiers in Curaçao, Aruba and Barbados. However, the Nations League format slated Curaçao and Jamaica to host their matches on the same night as Haiti’s, shunting Haiti to Sabina Park, the home of the Jamaica national team until their current venue opened in 1962. Now a cricket ground, Sabina Park hosted two of Haiti’s Nations League qualifiers.History comes home as St Louis City top Columbus Crew to win US Open CupRead moreWhile the shuffle sends Haiti within their opponents’ borders, they couldn’t have found a more hospitable home away from home. Miami boasts by far the largest population of Haitians and their descendants in the US, with nearly half a million concentrated predominantly in south Florida. They will play at Nu Stadium, where they played the venue’s first international friendly – a pre-World Cup clash with Peru – in June before a sold-out crowd of 26,700. That support dwarfed the crowds they drew at Sabina Park, where their two matches attracted an average of 297 fans.The US have won four of their six clashes with Haiti this century, with the other two matches ending in draws.This will be Haiti’s first trip back to the US since this summer’s World Cup, a hero-making turn for the Caribbean nation in their first tournament appearance since 1974. The Grenadiers were handed a difficult group, losing all three games against Morocco, Scotland and Brazil. Nonetheless, theyenjoyed fantastic support from fansat their matches in Massachusetts, Philadelphia and Atlanta.The second leg of the quarter-final is set to take place on 17 November at TQL Stadium in Cincinnati.Concacaf added that “this flexibility will remain in place for as long as the security situation in Haiti persists”. Haiti, as well as clubs based in the country, will need to seek approval from Concacaf for each match they look to play in “the territory of its opponents”, a separate arrangement from the neutral sites they have previously booked. The confederation stipulated that the measure “may be amended or withdrawn by the Concacaf Council at any time”.Explore more on these topicsHaiti football teamUSAUS sportsShareReuse this content

title: Six-year ban for top marathon runner who submitted fake prescription | Marathon | The Guardian
description: One of the world’s leading marathon runners, Ruti Aga, has been banned for six years after anti-doping investigators found she submitted a fake prescription to explain a failed drug test
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: One of the world’s leading marathon runners, Ruti Aga, has been banned for six years after anti-doping investigators found she submitted a fake prescription to explain a failed drug test
Content: Ruti Aga with her Tokyo marathon 2019 gold medal. The Ethiopian athlete tested positive for a banned substance after winning a half-marathon in China in March.Photograph: Issei Kato/ReutersView image in fullscreenRuti Aga with her Tokyo marathon 2019 gold medal. The Ethiopian athlete tested positive for a banned substance after winning a half-marathon in China in March.Photograph: Issei Kato/ReutersMarathonSix-year ban for top marathon runner who submitted fake prescriptionClinic named by Ruti Aga did not exist, testers foundPrescription signed by a family member, not a doctorAssociated PressThu 22 Oct 2026 08.13 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleOne of the world’s leading marathon runners, Ruti Aga, has been banned for six years after anti-doping investigators found she submitted a fake prescription to explain a failed drug test.The Ethiopian athlete won the Tokyo marathon in 2019 and has reached the podium at the Berlin and New York marathons. She tested positive for the banned substance methylprednisolone after winning a half-marathon in China in March, theAthleticsIntegrity Unit said on Thursday.Athletics wishes it could scrub the women’s marathon world record – what can be done? | Sean IngleRead moreAga said she had been given the substance by a doctor in Ethiopia to treat knee pain, but the AIU said it found the clinic named on the document did not exist and the supposed prescription had been signed by a family member who was not a registered doctor.After that, Aga failed to respond to charges for the use of methylprednisolone and “tampering” with the anti-doping process, the AIU added, meaning the six-year ban was issued without a hearing. The 32-year-old runner’s ban includes two years for the use of the substance and four more for tampering.Explore more on these topicsMarathonDrugs in sportAthleticsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Emery and Nagelsmann are top targets if Manchester United sack Carrick | Manchester United | The Guardian
description: Unai Emery and Julian Nagelsmann have emerged as leading targets to replace Michael Carrick as Manchester United’s manager
Author: Jamie Jackson
Headline: Unai Emery and Julian Nagelsmann have emerged as leading targets to replace Michael Carrick as Manchester United’s manager
Content: Unai Emery (left) and Julian Nagelsmann are in the frame if the Manchester United job becomes available.Composite: Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenUnai Emery (left) and Julian Nagelsmann are in the frame if the Manchester United job becomes available.Composite: Getty ImagesManchester UnitedEmery and Nagelsmann are top targets if Manchester United sack CarrickCarrick expected to be in charge for Bournemouth gameCompensation could be obstacle for Aston Villa’s EmeryJamie JacksonThu 22 Oct 2026 11.06 EDTLast modified on Thu 22 Oct 2026 14.08 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleUnai Emery and Julian Nagelsmann have emerged as leading targets to replace Michael Carrick as Manchester United’s head coach should the board decide on a change after the club’s poorest start to the season since 1986.Carrick is expected to remain in place for Sunday’s visit of Bournemouth – he is due to hold his pre-game media conference on Friday – but the 45-year-old’s job is in the balance after two wins from 11 games this season.Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation at Comoin the Champions League has focused attention at United on a potential candidate to succeed Carrick should he be removed. Emery and Nagelsmann have admirers at board level.Carrick joins Wilcox under the bus after Manchester United’s latest night in crisis | Max RushdenRead moreEmery is contracted to Aston Villa until 2029, and Nagelsmann is unemployed after leaving his position as Germany’s manager in the wake of the team’slast-32 World Cup exitin the summer.Emery has impressed since taking over Villa in 2022, last season winning the Europa League, the club’s first major trophy since 1996, and finishing fourth, one place behind United.But Emery earns between £10m and £12m a year, so the compensation package United would have to pay Villa may be a stumbling block. He has also won trophies with Sevilla, Paris Saint-Germain and Villarreal and had a less successful spell with Arsenal.Nagelsmann has managed Hoffenheim, RB Leipzig and Bayern Munich, with whom he won the Bundesliga in 2022 before being sacked in March 2023. He is highly regarded by United’s head of recruitment, Christopher Vivell.The 39-year-old Nagelsmann guided Germany to the Euro 2024 quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by the eventual winners, Spain. It is understood Nagelsmann would be interested in an approach from United.Other potential candidates who may be considered include Antonio Conte, Eddie Howe and Kieran McKenna. They are out of work after leaving jobs with Napoli, Newcastle and Ipswich respectively. It is understood Fabian Hürzeler is not open to leaving Brighton at this stage.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBruno Fernandes’s house was the target of a break-in while United’s captain was away with the team at the Como defeat. His family were not at home, it is understood, and the intruders were inside for less than five minutes before the police arrived.The club is supporting Fernandes and his family and have asked for privacy regarding what it said was a difficult time.Meanwhile, the 32-year-old midfielder is not expected to face any disciplinary action for his criticism of Carrick on Wednesday.Fernandes questioned the head coach’s tacticsfollowing the Como defeat.Explore more on these topicsManchester UnitedUnai EmerynewsShareReuse this content

title: Europa League: Celtic lose to Celta after leading, Mateta returns in Palace draw | Europa League | The Guardian
description: Celtic fell to another defeat after taking the lead against Celta Vigo, while Jean-Philippe Mateta scored on his first start for Crystal Palace since the opening day in a 2-2 draw at Besiktas
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Celtic fell to another defeat after taking the lead against Celta Vigo, while Jean-Philippe Mateta scored on his first start for Crystal Palace since the opening day in a 2-2 draw at Besiktas
Content: Celta Vigo's Javi Rodríguez shows his delight after giving his side the lead at Celtic Park.Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PAView image in fullscreenCelta Vigo's Javi Rodríguez shows his delight after giving his side the lead at Celtic Park.Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PAEuropa LeagueEuropa League: Celtic lose to Celta after leading, Mateta returns in Palace drawSunderland drop points in 1-1 draw but stay unbeatenVAR rules out Juventus winner in draw with RennesAgenciesThu 22 Oct 2026 17.41 EDTFirst published on Thu 22 Oct 2026 15.14 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleCelticsuffered moreEuropa Leaguepain as Spanish sideCelta Vigocame from behind to win 2-1 at Parkhead. After defeats by Ferencvaros and Benfica in their first two league phase fixtures, Martin O’Neill’s side struggled to impose themselves on the visitors who were neat and tidy without really testing Hoops keeper Sam Johnstone.Germany midfielder Mika Baur fired the home side in front just over a minute into the second half to thrill theCelticfans but Spain defender Javi Rodríguez scored twice in three minutes – a header then an unstoppable drive – to stun the home side who could not find a way back.Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather stormRead moreIt was another damaging Euro night for the Scottish champions, knocked out of the Champions League qualifiers by LASK on a 5-4 aggregate after being 4-0 up at one stage earlier in the season.Celtic’s ultras group, the Green Brigade, boycotted the game in protest at the running of the club, albeit there appeared to be only a couple of hundred empty seats, while 3,000 raucous Celta Vigo fans helped the noise.Jean-Philippe Mateta scored on his first start since the opening day butCrystalPalacecould not capitalise on aBesiktasred card to produce a winner in their 2-2 Europa League draw in Istanbul.Palace were looking to bounce back from Sunday’s humiliating 5-0 defeat at Brighton, and were the superior side before Wilfred Ndidi opened the scoring for the hosts in first-half stoppage time.Yéremy Pino drew the sides level six minutes after the restart and Mateta – who had a first-half goal chalked off by the video assistant referee – fired Palace to a first-time lead four minutes later.Junior Olaitan netted a 73rd-minute equaliser, and Palace could not find a winner after Umit Akdag was sent off for a clumsy 77th-minute challenge on Jørgen Strand Larsen, who was subsequently forced off.Sunderland’s winning start in the Europa League was ended with a 1-1 draw away toLech Poznan. The point keeps Sunderland unbeaten in Europe this season after back-to-back victories over AZ Alkmaar and Torreense.In a thrilling openingSunderlandwent in front early through Timur Tutierov, who was making only his third competitive start since arriving at Sunderland’s academy in 2023.The visitors had opportunities to extend their lead when Malick Fofana hit the post and Nordi Mukiele forced a strong save from Mateusz Lis, but Lech responded in the 70th minute through the substitute Leo Bengtsson’s low strike.Bournemouth v Milan, Celtic v Celta Vigo, and more: Europa League – liveRead moreRégis Le Bris made six changes fromSunday’s Premier League defeat to Bournemouth, including a first start of the season for Habib Diarra following his return from injury.Sunderland took the lead in the second minute when Nilson Angulo pounced on a tame pass from Lis, and the winger crossed into Tutierov in the middle of the box to comfortably nod home for his first Sunderland goal.Robin Roefs was called into action at the opposite end with a double save to deny Patrik Wålemark and palm away Antoni Kozubal’s header before Diarra charged up the pitch and fired into the side netting.The hosts had two good chances to level when Pablo Rodríguez blasted just past the post and Daniel Håkans was played through in a one-on-one with Roefs but flicked his shot wide.Sunderland enjoyed a good spell of possession during which the skipper, Granit Xhaka, had a strike parried away by Lis and the rebound fell to Fofana, who rattled the woodwork. Moments later Dayann Méthalie was denied at the near post by Lis as the visitors pushed for a second goal.View image in fullscreenTimur Tutierov scores his third goal for Sunderland’s first team since joining the academy in 2023.Photograph: Wojtek Radwański/AFP/Getty ImagesEarly in the second half, Fofana cut into the box but could only send his effort over and Poznan looked to strike when Wålemark scuffed a shot wide following a good solo run.Diarra fired wide for and Angulo’s low strike was scooped up by Lis, who moments later made a great save to tip Mukiele’s shot over the bar.Bengtsson looked to make an instant impact from the bench when his effort from Wålemark’s cross was sent wide. However, the midfielder made no mistake when next presented with an opportunity as a corner rebounded towards him just inside the area and he fired into the bottom corner with 20 minutes to play.Poznan almost took the lead moments later when Roefs made a brilliant point-blank stop from Michal Gurgul. Fofana skewed an effort wide as Sunderland looked to restore their advantage and the substitute Chris Rigg’s powerful shot landed on the roof of the net, but the spoils were shared.Quick GuideConference League: Salah breaks Hearts and Brighton held by JablonecShowInjury-hitHeartsproduced a spirited display in Turkey but ultimately went down to a 2-0 Conference League defeat at the hands of Mohamed Salah-inspiredTrabzonspor.The Scottish side acquitted themselves well amid a hostile atmosphere before going down to Salah’s first-half penalty and a second-half strike from Franculino, laid on by the former Liverpool star (pictured).The defeat leaves Wouter Vrancken’s side with one point from two matches ahead of their trip to Swiss champions Thun in a fortnight. Their visit had started in painful fashion after left-back Harry Milne suffered a suspected anterior cruciate ligament injury during training.Brightondrew a rare blank as they were held to a goalless draw by Czech minnowsJablonec. The Premier League’s top scorers, who have scored 23 goals across their first seven matches, misfired badly in the foothills of the Jizera Mountains in northern Czechia.Brighton head coach Fabian Hürzeler, in his 100th match in charge, made eight changes from that memorable win with only Bart Verbruggen, Olivier Boscagli and Pascal Gross keeping their places. The visitors squandered a host of chances, the best falling to Jack Hinshelwood, Georginio Rutter and Ibrahim Osman, and Jablonec were looking the likelier to score towards the end.Antonín Rusek almost capitalised on a mistake by Joao Costinha before Verbruggen had to make a spectacular fingertip save to prevent Jiri Slama’s drive from hitting the top corner.Press AssociationPhotograph: Hasan Tascan/AnadoluWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Juventusdropped their first points of the Europa League campaign after coming ⁠from behind to draw 2-2 with visitorsRennes.Zeki Celik gave Juventus a fifth-minute lead, but ⁠the French side ⁠kept their ​composure and were level 10 minutes later when the Jordan international Musa Al-Taamari finished from close range for ⁠his first goal in the competition.Rennes then stunned the hosts with a Boulaye Dia penalty two minutes before the ⁠break as the Italians struggled to create chances until Nick Woltemade equalised ​from the spot in the 67th ‌minute.View image in fullscreenNick Woltemade equalises from the spot for Juventus in their 2-2 draw with Rennes.Photograph: sportinfoto/DeFodi Images/ShutterstockThe Germany forward ‌twice went close to scoring again as Luciano Spalletti’s team upped the ‌pressure, and Juve thought they had won it in the 88th minute when Jhon Lucumí found the net from close range, but his effort was ruled out for offside.The draw at least spared Juventus a second successive defeat following Sunday’s 3-0 home loss to Lazio ‌in Serie A.Jonas Hofmann made the most of his surprise start forBayer Leverkusen, scoring twice in three minutes ​to give the Bundesliga side a 2-0 victory atOFI Creteto go top of the table with their third straight win.Crete, who stunned Hoffenheim 2-0 in their opening league-phase match, were twice caught napping by Hofmann, ⁠who was added to the side following an injury to ​Martin Terrier. Leverkusen have ​nine points and leadFerencvaros​on goal difference after the Hungarian side beatTorreense​4-1.Explore more on these topicsEuropa LeagueCelticCrystal PalaceSunderlandJuventusRennesLech PoznanShareReuse this content

title: Bruno Guimarães had sleepless nights before Newcastle exit but hopes for same ‘love’ at Arsenal | Arsenal | The Guardian
description: Midfielder says there were a lot of tears as he said goodbye at St James’ Park but he is enjoying the remorselessness at his new club
Author: David Hytner
Headline: Midfielder says there were a lot of tears as he said goodbye at St James’ Park but he is enjoying the remorselessness at his new club
Content: ‘We don’t accept a draw at Bayern,’ says Arsenal’s Bruno Guimarães.Photograph: David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreen‘We don’t accept a draw at Bayern,’ says Arsenal’s Bruno Guimarães.Photograph: David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesArsenalBruno Guimarães had sleepless nights before Newcastle exit but hopes for same ‘love’ at ArsenalMidfielder says there were a lot of tears as he said goodbye at St James’ Park but he is enjoying the remorselessness at his new clubDavid Hytnerin MunichThu 22 Oct 2026 10.00 EDTLast modified on Thu 22 Oct 2026 14.16 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFor Bruno Guimarães, it was a time to show his steeliness, to fix his eyes on the prize – even if he knew it would surely mean them welling up. And then some. It was a tumultuous summer for the Brazil midfielder. A fine World Cup on a personal level was marred by a crucial penalty miss inthe last-16 loss against Norway. Now he had the dream move lined up to Arsenal but it could not happen without breaking some hearts at Newcastle.Guimarães admits he lay awake at night as the emotions swirled. How could he leave Newcastle, the club where he made so many connections and enjoyed so many highs after joiningfrom Lyon in January 2022? There were the Champions League qualifications and, above all, theCarabao Cup triumph in 2025that ended a 70-year wait for a domestic trophy. On the other hand, how could he resist Arsenal and the prospect of competing regularly for the game’s top honours?‘It doesn’t look good’: Arteta concerned as Saka limps off against Bayern MunichRead moreSometimes, you simply have to take a deep breath and the plunge. Nobody wants to die wondering. Guimarães knew the Newcastle team was breaking up. Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali had gone to Barcelona and Tottenham. The manager, Eddie Howe, was at the end of the line andwould also leave. Guimarães went through withthe £75m transferand nobody can say it has not worked out so far.Arsenal felt he would provide a different element for them, different ways of unlocking defences, plus his trademark work rate and snarl. Guimarães has brought all of that. Already he has made a difference. He even gave a little back to Newcastle when he scored his first Arsenal goalat Sunderland in September, paving the way for a 2-0 victory. Two Premier League games later, he scored the winnerat home against Leeds.Guimarães almost got another vital goal on Wednesday in the Champions League tie at Bayern Munich only for Manuel Neuer to deny him with an outrageous save. That would have put Arsenal 2-1 up.The game finished 2-2, Arsenal fighting until the end and equalising through Declan Rice in the 82nd minute. Still, it has not been easy for Guimarães and he surely has Arsenal’s visit to Newcastle on 21 November circled in his diary. His greatest hope is that he can build the same relationships at his new club.“It was not just hard to tell Eddie but to tell the owners and my teammates [about deciding to leave Newcastle],” Guimarães says. “But I think the club went to a new rotation; a lot of players left, as well. The gaffer left. It was tough because my connection with the club was unbelievable. I never felt so loved like the way I was at Newcastle. I hope I can have the same love here atArsenal.View image in fullscreenBruno Guimarães says he had sleepless nights contemplating leaving Newcastle for Arsenal.Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters“It was hard for me to say bye. I remember when I said bye to the lads, I was crying. They were crying as well because we were a family there. I lost many, many nights of sleep because it was difficult for me, for my family. But sometimes in your life you have to make decisions and in my mind, I needed a new challenge. I wish Newcastle all the best because they were so nice to me. It is just time to move on and I’ve been enjoying my time here at Arsenal, as well.”Guimarães is enjoying his burgeoning midfield partnership with Rice, not to mention Martin Ødegaard, who tends to be the most advanced of the trio. That said, there is plenty of fluidity between the positions. There is the sense that the manager, Mikel Arteta, is searching for the perfect balance.“Declan can play – like me – as a No 6, No 8 or No 10,” Guimarães says. “The manager is still trying to get the best version of ourselves. Against Bayern, I played more as a No 6, Declan played more as a No 8. I enjoy playing with him a lot; with Martin, as well. We have been on a good run so far.”Guimarães’ battles when he was at Newcastle against Rice have been well documented. He said Rice had messaged him as he prepared to sign for Arsenal, saying: “No more fights, now we’re friends.” Guimarães is the player you loathe when he is against you but love when he is in your ranks.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenManuel Neuer keeps out Bruno Guimarães’s header in the Champions League.Photograph: Michael Zemanek/ShutterstockWhat was the worst thing Guimarães said to Rice when they were in opposition? “It is difficult to say,” he replies with a smile. “I am like this when I play against teams. When we were playing against each other, I was not nice to him, he was not nice to me! Now we try to help each other on the pitch.”Guimarães cannot believe how Neuer kept out his close-range header; the 40-year-old goalkeeper clawed the ball up against the crossbar and away. “He pulled off a miracle,” Guimarães says. “I asked him after the game: ‘How did you manage to save that?’ He said: ‘I don’t know. I just saved it!’ He’s unbelievable, one of the best keepers in the world. No matter how old he is, he is top.”What Guimarães has seen with clarity is the remorselessness of the collective attitude at Arsenal; the insatiable will to win, which comes from Arteta. Next up for them is Everton at home on Saturday. Guimarães knows he is in the right place.“The mentality of the club has changed a lot and Arteta shows this perfectly,” Guimarães says. “We don’t accept a draw at Bayern. We always want to win. That is the mentality that we go to the training ground with every day. Arteta is always a little bit addicted to videos and the way that he can make us feel better on the pitch. We have a top manager with a top mentality. We want to win everything possible.”Explore more on these topicsArsenalfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Harry Kane says wait to learn if he has won Ballon d’Or is stressful for family | Harry Kane | The Guardian
description: Harry Kane would love to know now whether he has won the Ballon d’Or because the uncertainty and questions are driving his family to distraction
Author: David Hytner
Headline: Harry Kane would love to know now whether he has won the Ballon d’Or because the uncertainty and questions are driving his family to distraction
Content: Harry Kane scored his 16th goal of the season against Arsenal on Wednesday. Last season he got 61 for Bayern Munich and 12 for England.Photograph: Alex Grimm/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenHarry Kane scored his 16th goal of the season against Arsenal on Wednesday. Last season he got 61 for Bayern Munich and 12 for England.Photograph: Alex Grimm/Getty ImagesHarry KaneHarry Kane says wait to learn if he has won Ballon d’Or is stressful for familyBayern Munich and England striker is odds-on favourite‘I try not to think about it. Obviously it is hard not to’David Hytnerin MunichThu 22 Oct 2026 05.13 EDTLast modified on Thu 22 Oct 2026 15.39 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleHarry Kane would love to know now whether he has won the Ballon d’Or because the uncertainty and constant questions are driving his family to distraction. But theBayern Munichand England striker accepts the ­suspense before the big reveal at the London Palladium on Monday night is part of the show.Kane is the odds-on favourite to win the prestigious individual ­honour after a prolific run of form. The 33-year-old scored 61 goals for Bayern last season and 12 for England. This time out, he has 10 for Bayern and six for England.He scored from the penalty spot in Wednesday’s2-2 Champions League draw against Arsenalat the Allianz Arena, although his standout moment was the inch-perfect through ball that set up Alphonso Davies to make it 1-1.Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal is the second-favourite for the Ballon d’Or and Kylian Mbappé of Real Madrid is next in the betting.“I think my wife would prefer to know and my family … it’s very stressful for everyone,” Kane said. “I can see why they don’t tell people. They want everyone to go, all the big names, and there will be more people watching it if they don’t know so I can understand why.“From my point of view, I’d love to know to just kind of see and not have to wait throughout the whole night. But it is their decision, I can’t control that. We’ll have to just enjoy it and try not to stress out too much.“I try not to think about it. ­Obviously it is hard not to. There are always rumours and stuff flying around so you try to stay away from it.”View image in fullscreenLuis Díaz suffered injury after making an appearance from the bench for Bayern Munich against Arsenal.Photograph: Tiego Grenho/Every Second Media/ShutterstockKane’s fellow Bayern forward Luis Díaz will be out ⁠of action for the “foreseeable future” after suffering a minor muscle ⁠tear in his ⁠left ​hamstring during Wednesday’s game.The 29-year-old Colombia international came on in the ⁠68th minute at the Allianz Arena but ​was forced off ‌in stoppage ‌time after suffering the injury.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionExaminations carried out ‌by Bayern’s medical staff confirmed the hamstring tear, the club said in a statement. “The 29-year-old forward will therefore be sidelined for the time being,” Bayern said.Reuters contributed to this reportExplore more on these topicsHarry KaneBallon d'OrBayern MunichnewsShareReuse this content

title: Enzo Maresca says honest talks have revitalised Foden’s Manchester City form  | Manchester City | The Guardian
description: Enzo Maresca has revealed he held heart-to-heart conversations with Phil Foden to help the midfielder back to his best
Author: Will Unwin
Headline: Enzo Maresca has revealed he held heart-to-heart conversations with Phil Foden to help the midfielder back to his best
Content: Phil Foden scored a hat-trick against AEK Athens in Manchester City’s 5-1 Champions League win on Tuesday.Photograph: MI News/NurPhoto/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenPhil Foden scored a hat-trick against AEK Athens in Manchester City’s 5-1 Champions League win on Tuesday.Photograph: MI News/NurPhoto/ShutterstockManchester CityEnzo Maresca says honest talks have revitalised Foden’s Manchester City formPlayer has scored four goals in last two games for CityAston Villa the next test for Premier League leadersWill UnwinThu 22 Oct 2026 07.36 EDTLast modified on Thu 22 Oct 2026 14.42 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleEnzo Maresca has revealed he held heart-to-heart conversations withPhil Fodento help the midfielder back to his best. Foden has struggled over the past two years but has scored four goals in his past two games to give hope he can recapture the form that won him the Professional Footballers’ Association player of the year award in 2023-24.City travel to Aston Villa on Saturday lunchtime aiming to continue their perfect Premier League start under Maresca, with Erling Haaland fit after sitting on the bench forWednesday’s Champions League win over AEK Athens.“Since we started I sat down with Phil two or three times, especially at the beginning,” said Maresca, who knew Foden from a spell as Pep Guardiola’s assistant. “Maybe love is not the right word to use but just to show him how important he is.“I said many times that I know Phil from years ago so I know how good he is. For different reasons the last few years he was not good enough, but again I think when you have more players like Phil available you are a better team because at the end it’s a matter of improving players. If you improve the players you improve the team, so for me it’s my duty to try to help Phil to be again one of the best players in England. But it’s not just about one game – the season is very long.”Foden, 26, needs to remain consistent to keep his place in the team, with plenty of competition for the attacking roles, including from Rayan Cherki, who Maresca has described as “one of the best players in Europe”.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionCity’s only competitive defeat under Maresca cameagainst Paris Saint-Germainin the Champions League, and they have seven straight wins in the Premier League to sitthree points clearat the top. Maresca is waiting to find out whether Matheus Nunes, Mateo Kovacic and Nico O’Reilly are available after missing the AEK game. “The mood is good, we are happy with our start but we are still hungry for more wins,” Maresca said.Explore more on these topicsManchester CityPhil FodennewsShareReuse this content

title: Cathinka Tandberg: ‘Spurs fans hate Arsenal. That’s how it is’ | Women's football | The Guardian
description: Norwegian forward might look to Harry Kane for inspiration on the pitch, but when north London derby comes around, she needs no lessons on what the rivalry means
Author: Sophie Downey
Headline: Norwegian forward might look to Harry Kane for inspiration on the pitch, but when north London derby comes around, she needs no lessons on what the rivalry means
Content: Cathinka Tandberg celebrates scoring against Aston Villa this season.Photograph: Richard Pelham/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenCathinka Tandberg celebrates scoring against Aston Villa this season.Photograph: Richard Pelham/Getty ImagesMoving the Goalposts newsletterWomen's footballCathinka Tandberg: ‘Spurs fans hate Arsenal. That’s how it is’Norwegian forward might look to Harry Kane for inspiration on the pitch, but when north London derby comes around, she needs no lessons on what the rivalry meansSophie DowneyThu 22 Oct 2026 06.44 EDTLast modified on Thu 22 Oct 2026 14.06 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on Google“It means more than just three points. It’s for the whole club. It’s for the whole place. It’s for the whole of Tottenham.” One only needs to be in the presence of Tottenham Hotspur’s Cathinka Tandberg for a few minutes to feel the passion that emanates from her when it comes to this weekend’s north London derby. As a lifelong Spurs fan, the forward understands more than most the intensity of the rivalry that exists between her side and Arsenal, one that she cannot wait to experience once again on Saturday.“It will just be an incredible feeling,” she tells Moving the Goalposts. “I think you will feel a few nerves that you maybe don’t feel in a normal game but that’s good.”“All the Spurs fans hate Arsenal and Arsenal hate Spurs. That’s how it is. You want to show that you’re the best team. Simple as that. You just want to fight for the club, the badge and for the people around you.”View image in fullscreenCathinka Tandberg joined Tottenham from the Swedish side Hammarby in the summer of 2025.Photograph: Javier García/Tottenham Hotspur FC/ShutterstockIt has been a significant 13 months for the 22-year-old who made her dream move to London in September 2025. After catching the eye as a goalscorer in the Damallsvenskan at first Linköping and then Hammarby, the Norwegian was signed by Martin Ho on deadline day to bolster the team’s attacking options. She made her mark on her first start, scoring a spectacular 40-yard goal against Everton.“I settled really well,” she reflects. “I’m really enjoying it and want to push myself forward. It’s been a tough start [to this season] and I haven’t really got what I wanted. But there’s loads of games left. I’m still young. I’m still improving and learning. I just have to trust the process and trust what I’m surrounded by.”“It’s a big difference from Sweden,” she continues. “You meet World Cup players week in, week out so you have to perform every week if you want results. I feel like my physicality has changed a lot. I’ve got stronger and fitter. Playing under Martin has made me think more away from the goals. I think more about how I play with the ball, how I press and all of those things that I maybe didn’t focus on before … it’s a bit like Harry Kane. The older he gets, he has developed his game as well. He needed to be deeper in the pitch because that’s how they wanted to play and then he has to be better with the ball. That’s a bit how I also need to be. I can’t only just stand in the box. I need to be good everywhere else.”Spurs have been transformed under Ho and finished fifth last season. However, with success, comes expectation, ambitions that Tandberg clearly shares but with a sense of perspective.“Tottenham has always been a Champions League club for me,” she says. “But I’m a fan so I can’t really talk for the other players. When I came to the club, I said that I want to get top three. But you also need to be realistic and to see where the team has been before. The transformation that Martin has done in a season is unbelievable. I don’t think anyone else could do that. That tells you everything about him. He’s one of the greatest coaches I’ve worked with and I think everyone that comes here, one of the reasons is because of him. We all trust him and the process.”View image in fullscreen‘Tottenham has always been a Champions League club for me. But I’m a fan so I can’t really talk for the other players. When I came to the club, I said that I want to get top three. But you also need to be realistic and to see where the team has been before.’ Cathinka Tandberg’s ambitions for her club are high.Photograph: Leila Coker/WSL/WSL Football/Getty ImagesThat faith is currently being tested. After an unbeaten start, Tottenham have suffered back-to-back defeats, shipping six goals to both London City Lionesses and Chelsea.“You can call it a dip in form but I still feel like we also showed our qualities in those games,” Tandberg says. “It’s just about ourselves. We maybe need to change our mentality a bit, find that fire and dig a bit deeper when we play those top teams. I feel like maybe it’s good that it’s come because it had to at some point. It’s about how we respond.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion‘We also have to realise where this team has been. Two years ago, it was a relegation club. We need to realise how quickly it has [changed]. But, of course, we have expectations and levels that we want to come to and we know that we can. I feel like we’re working so well … we just have to believe in everyone.”For Tandberg, putting that right against a struggling Arsenal in front a home crowd would be the perfect tonic. “I’ve always been a passionate player and I’ve been a supporter,” she says. “I play for the supporters because I just enjoy it and I know how it is to be in the stands. I think [that connection] is very important because we have their back and they have ours. To give them something back is important and to show that we see and hear them every time.”Get in touchIf you have any questions or comments about any of our newsletters please emailmoving.goalposts@theguardian.com.This is an extract from our free email about women’s football, Moving the Goalposts. title: Lewis Hamilton aims to extend career till early 2030s so he can race in African Grand Prix | Formula One 2026 | The Guardian
description: The 41-year-old is set on fulfilling his ‘dream to be able to race in Africa’, specifically Rwanda which will host despite criticism of its human rights record
Author: Giles Richards
Headline: The 41-year-old is set on fulfilling his ‘dream to be able to race in Africa’, specifically Rwanda which will host despite criticism of its human rights record
Content: Lewis Hamilton believes that the race in Rwanda will be a force for good rather than sportswashing.Photograph: Brett Farmer/LAT ImagesView image in fullscreenLewis Hamilton believes that the race in Rwanda will be a force for good rather than sportswashing.Photograph: Brett Farmer/LAT ImagesFormula One 2026Lewis Hamilton aims to extend career till early 2030s so he can race in African Grand Prix41-year-old set on ‘dream to be able to race in Africa’Rwanda to host despite criticism of human rights recordGiles Richardsin AustinThu 22 Oct 2026 17.53 EDTLast modified on Thu 22 Oct 2026 18.33 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleLewis Hamilton has said he hopes to remain racing in Formula One until he can take part in the African Grand Prix which isset to take place in Rwanda in the 2030s. The seven-time world champion believes it is right that F1 is to hold a race there despite criticism of the country’s human rights record.Last week F1 confirmed Rwanda was to host the African Grand Prix having concluded a 10-year agreement for the meeting on a purpose-built circuit, with the first race set for the early 2030s. It is lined up to be held on a circuit in Bugesera, 25 miles south of the capital, Kigali, which has yet to be constructed and marks a return to the African continent for the first time since it last held a race at Kyalami, SouthAfricain 1993.Austin GP is about much more than potential for Antonelli’s first F1 world title | Giles RichardsRead moreHamilton has beenchampioning a race in Africafor some time. The 41-year-old is understood to be currently contracted with Ferrari until the end of the 2027 season, and speaking before this weekend’s US Grand Prix he said he would like to continue racing for at least another four years in order to make it to the meeting in Rwanda.“I’m now forced to have to stay a lot longer because we have a race in Africa andthat’s been my dreamto be able to race in Africa,” he said. “So, I have to keep fighting to try and stay fit if I can. If I can still punch out good results over the next year, we’ll keep it going.”Hamilton would be at least in his mid-40s if he was to continue until 2030. F1’s current oldest driver is 45-year-old Fernando Alonso.F1’s deal withRwandais for a 10-year period but because of the country’s human rights record the award of the race has been criticised as an act of sportswashing.Quick GuideBritain's Slater, 18, to make F1 practice debut for AudiShowBritain’s 18-year-old Freddie Slater will make his Formula 1 free practice debut for ⁠Audi at next week’s Mexico City Grand Prix.Audi entered Formula 1 this year ⁠after taking over ⁠the ​Sauber team, and Slater was the first driver signed to the team’s new driver academy.Slater ⁠finished second in the Formula 3 standings to Ugo Ugochukwu in his debut season while ⁠racing for Trident Motorsport. He is slated to move ​to Formula 2 with Invicta ‌next year."Getting behind the wheel of an F1 car at a grand prix weekend is a big moment for me and something I’ve been dreaming of since I was a kid," Slater said. “I’ve learned a ‌lot this year, and these Free practice outings with Audi F1 Team will be another opportunity ​to keep gaining on-track experience."Slater is also slated to drive in the first practice session at next month’s Sao Paulo Grand Prix."We have seen Freddie making great progress ⁠throughout recent years, both on and off the track; ​it is ​the right time for ​Freddie to step up," Audi racing director and ​academy director ‌Allan McNish, a former F1 driver himself, said."These ​appearances ​in Mexico and Brazil will give him valuable experience of a Formula 1 race weekend, and another chance to continue his development."ReutersWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.“A 10-year grand prix ‘presented by Visit Rwanda’ is a sportswashing prize for the Rwandan authorities,” said Felix Jakens, Amnesty UK’s head of campaigns. “Rwanda isbuying into the world’s biggest sportsto polish its image and deflect from ⁠its appalling human rights record. Formula One says sport can be ‘a positive force for good’. That rings hollow if F1 shrugs off who it is partnering with. Rwanda’s authorities are prolific in arbitrary detention, torture and the repression of free speech.”View image in fullscreenRwanda’s investment in sports sponsorship has led to accusations that it is attempting to sportswash its human rights record.Photograph: SOPA Images/LightRocket/Getty ImagesHamilton nonetheless felt the meeting would serve as a force for good in Africa and that there also should be more education about the continent.“I’m really, really hopeful for that grand prix,” he said. “Of course, I don’t get to choose where we go, and naturally there’s problems all over the world today, so I’ve seen many of the stories but I think we really have to approach it with humility.“There’s a lot that we don’t know. I mean, growing up in England, they never ever taught us anything about Africa. It needs to be on the curriculum. A lot of the problems they have there are still results of colonialism, and the West intervening.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe RecapThe best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“I really hope, and I still have hopes, that Africa unites. I know there’s many people that don’t want that to happen, because they would be so powerful if they did, but I’m still hopeful that at some stage they will.”The new race is being backed by the government of Rwanda and the Rwanda Development Board, who intend to develop the venue as a destination not only for motorsport but for promoting economic growth. The country has recently invested heavily in hosting sporting events, including cycling’s road world championships, cricket’s Women’s Challenge Trophy, the 2023 Fifa congress andthe Basketball Africa League.Hamilton felt that at least the race would present an opportunity for people to take a greater interest in Africa.“Going doesn’t mean that you neglect the things that are happening there,” he said. “Hopefully many people start to educate themselves a little bit more of what is happening there, what has happened there for hundreds of years and I hope that does spark the conversation. Then I guess I’ll finish it off with, I think we need to make sure we’re pushing to free Congo, free Sudan, free Syria, free Palestine. I think there’s a lot of peace that I’m hoping that at some stage we get to.”Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli goes into this weekend’s US Grand Prix in a position to clinch his first F1 title. The 20-year-old holds a 102-point lead over his teammate George Russell and will become Formula One’s youngest world champion if he wins, Russell finishes ninth or lower and Hamilton is fifth or lower.Explore more on these topicsFormula One 2026Lewis HamiltonFerrariFormula OneMotor sportRwandaAfricanewsShareReuse this content

title: McDermott blames Rugby League World Cup format as England face exit | Rugby League World Cup 2026 | The Guardian
description: Brian McDermott has conceded England’s hopes of reaching the Rugby League World Cup semi-finals may already be over, blaming the tournament’s format and their opening loss to Tonga
Author: Aaron Bower
Headline: Brian McDermott has conceded England’s hopes of reaching the Rugby League World Cup semi-finals may already be over, blaming the tournament’s format and their opening loss to Tonga
Content: England’s Victor Radley, flanked by his England teammates, registers the shock of defeat by Tonga, effectively ending their hopes.Photograph: Joel Carrett/EPAView image in fullscreenEngland’s Victor Radley, flanked by his England teammates, registers the shock of defeat by Tonga, effectively ending their hopes.Photograph: Joel Carrett/EPARugby League World Cup 2026McDermott blames Rugby League World Cup format as England face exitBig wins and help from Tonga needed to reach semi-finals‘You’ve got to hit the ground running, which we didn’t do’Aaron BowerThu 22 Oct 2026 08.41 EDTLast modified on Thu 22 Oct 2026 14.46 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBrian McDermott has conceded England’s hopes of reaching the Rugby League World Cup semi-finals may already be over, the head coach blaming the tournament’s format andtheir opening loss to Tonga.The World Cup has been reduced to 10 teams, down from 16 four years ago. That is largely due to financial reasons when the hosts, Australia, stepped in after France’s withdrawal. That has led to a unique format, with different levels of jeopardy for different countries based on their group.England are in the three-team Group B with the top two from a combined six-team table of Groups B and C progressing to the semi-finals. Defeat by Tonga last Saturday has made it difficult for England to qualify, with expected victories against France on Saturday and Papua New Guinea next week unlikely to be enough.PNG Chiefs unveil logo and jersey for first NRL season amid naming dispute with rival codeRead moreFor England to progress, Tonga must beat Samoa on 1 November and England need to win their two group games by a bigger margin than Samoa. McDermott conceded the odds are stacked against his side and was critical of the format.“The jeopardy of losing one game in a pool of three is so harsh, it’s almost like we don’t get another chance to straighten things out,” he said. “It’s just harsh that we have to take a standing eight count in that first round, but we’re ready to go again.“Nothing has gone wrong, it’s just a harsh competition in which you’ve got to hit the ground running, which we didn’t do.“I’m trying to be diplomatic here. If France held the World Cup, there would have been more teams in it and it would have been more like the usual format. I completely understand that if it has to be reduced to a 10-team competition.“It’s not the easiest thing to do and we end up with situations like this. If you lose one game, you don’t really get a chance to fix it. It’s tough because we now need to rely on other results if we are to go through.”In contrast, New Zealand are in the four-team Group A where two teams progress and despitelosing to Australia last weekwins over Fiji and Cook Islands will secure qualification.“New Zealand have lost their first game as well, but they’re going to get another go at it,” said McDermott. “The likelihood is that they’ll quality, their destiny is not lying in other people’s hands.”England have to inflict a second heavy defeat onLes Bleusafter France’s 78-4 loss to Samoa last Friday.England’s 30-12 defeat by Tonga drew criticism, but McDermott had promised his side would try to play a more enterprising brand of rugby. Also, England had been in Australia for less than a week, after a 48-hour journey from Manchester via London, Singapore and Sydney to reach their camp in Perth.View image in fullscreen‘If you lose one game, you don’t really get a chance to fix it,’ says the England head coach, Brian McDermott.Photograph: Anita Reca/SWpix.com/ShutterstockThat is perhaps why McDermott has resisted the temptation for wholesale changes, with the Warrington winger Matty Ashton replacing Zach Eckersley in the sole change to the starting lineup.England may be going home in a fortnight barring a minor miracle, but McDermott is upbeat about the national team’s long-term prospects. “I’m really pumped about what we’ve done over a short period of time; it’s been remarkable, really,” he said.“We’ve come together and looked pretty good. We’ve laid some foundations and we’re pretty excited about where this could go. I don’t think there’s a great need for change, just give me another three or four games with this mob.
